title: Dual-wavelength ALMA Observations of Dust Rings in Protoplanetary Disks
question: Do dust rings in three Taurus disks appear at the same locations and widths at 1.3 and 2.9 mm, and what do disk sizes, ring widths, spectral index and optical depth imply for dust trapping and grain growth?

data.bands: Band 3 (2.9 mm, new) and Band 6 (1.3 mm, previous)
data.sensitivity: RMS 12.8-16.5 uJy/beam at Band 3; 58.5-82.5 at Band 6

what.value: 1.3 mm Band 6 data, ring locations, inclinations/PAs priors

evidence.quote: identified from our previous 1.3 mm survey at 0.1$''$ resolution
Stellar mass and age are adopted from (cite: Long2019).
Spectral type is adopted from (cite: herczeg2014)

recipe.goal: Image Band 3 continuum and match resolution to Band 6
recipe.method: tclean mtmfs nterms=2, self-cal for GO/DL Tau, imsmooth to common beams

recipe.goal: Fit uv visibilities with parametric radial profiles
recipe.method: Galario synthetic visibilities, MCMC with emcee
key_parameters: 100 walkers, 5000 steps, last 1000 used; grid 0.0001-4" step 0.0005"
assumptions: axisymmetric profiles; Gaussian inner disk for DS Tau, tapered power law for GO/DL Tau, Gaussian rings

recipe.method: radius enclosing 95% (disk) or 68% (inner disk, cut at first local minimum) of model flux

recipe.goal: Compute spectral index, optical depth, beta
recipe.method: alpha from intensity profiles at two bands; tau from full Planck function with irradiated disk temperature
key_parameters: flaring angle 0.02, Td ~15 K at 50 au
assumptions: Td equals midplane irradiated temperature; absorption-dominated opacity

recipe.goal: Dust evolution modelling with pressure bump
recipe.method: Dust growth/fragmentation/drift model with planet-carved gap (Crida2006, Fung2014 corrections)
key_parameters: planet at 33 au, q=0.002, Rc=80 au, gamma=1, alpha=1e-3, vfrag=10 m/s, 180 size cells 1 um-2 m, 300 radial cells 1-300 au
assumptions: Gas-to-dust 100, 20% dust lost to drift, disk mass 5.8 MJup

answer_key.quantity: DS Tau ring width sigma at 1.3 mm
DS Tau ring width sigma at 2.9 mm
DS Tau 2.9 mm ring width, power-law inner disk model
Disk-integrated alpha_mm (DS Tau, GO Tau, DL Tau)

evidence.quote: 2.66, 2.58, and 2.40 for DS Tau, GO Tau, and DL Tau, respectively
the typical optical depth is about 0.1–0.2 for dust rings at 2.9 mm and 0.2–0.4 for dust rings at 1.3 mm

answer_key.quantity: Inner disk radius 2.9 mm vs 1.3 mm (DS Tau)

evidence.quote: The values for $R_{\rm inner,2.9mm}$ and $R_{\rm inner,1.3mm}$ are 11.7 and 15.5 au for DS Tau

answer_key.quantity: Model ring width from dust evolution (unconvolved)

evidence.quote: We therefore determine the ring width to be only 1.09 au at 2.9 mm and 1.29 au at 1.3 mm.

not_stated_but_needed: Band 6 (2016.1.01164.S) calibration, self-calibration and imaging details (reused from Long2018)
Image size, cell size, deconvolver details and masks for tclean
Exact uv-fit initial values and uv-binning/weighting handling
Dust model inputs for dust evolution code (code not named)
Whether spectral index is computed at matched beams or deprojected bins
missing_for_reproduction: Dust evolution code not named or released
score_reason: uv-fit recipe, priors and MCMC settings are well specified, but imaging details and the dust evolution code are missing and Band 6 processing is inherited.
rediscovery_reason: ALMA data are archival projects, the uv-fit recipe is mostly complete, and the main results are numeric tables (R95, ring widths).
